name: Individualism
summary: Political individualism puts the individual's autonomy and rights ahead of the demands of the state, institutions and social norms. Its mainstream, classical-liberal form holds that coercion is justified only to prevent harm to others, defends freedom of thought and unconventional ways of life, and distrusts both central direction and enforced conformity. Strands differ on property, welfare and whether any state is needed.
scope: The mainstream liberal individualist tradition: Locke, Mill's On Liberty, Tocqueville and Hayek's 'Individualism: True and False', as documented in the Wikipedia article and SEP entries on liberalism and libertarianism. Individualist anarchism (Stirner, Tucker), left-libertarian and new-liberal strands are noted but not the basis; many answers outside civil liberties and limited government are inferences and low confidence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Free exchange between individuals extends across borders in the classical liberal view; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Individualists reject class-based theories of exploitation and see exchange as mutually beneficial; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian strands defend property rights and freedom of association, while liberal strands accept anti-discrimination law; the mainstream leans toward freedom.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Liberal individualism protects individual rights against majorities through constitutional limits on government.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not a question the individualist tradition addresses; inferred as neutral since adherents are split between self-determination and respect for existing agreements.

elective-rulers.rationale: Locke-style consent theory makes legitimate rule depend on the consent of the governed, which favours elected over hereditary rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: Mainstream liberal individualism accepts bounded majority rule under constitutional limits; only individualist anarchists demand individual consent to every decision. Inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Lockean liberalism holds that a ruler who violates the law and the trust placed in him forfeits authority and may be resisted.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Liberalism historically favoured representative assemblies over arbitrary monarchs, though it also limits parliaments by rights; inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Individualists generally hold that suffering matters morally (Mill-style harm reasoning), though rights theory is split on animals; inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Property-respecting individualism usually accepts humane use of animals; inferred from property and harm principles.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Individualists favour voluntary charity but reject a status-based duty of the privileged; inferred from Hayek-style emphasis on equal rules.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Mill prizes active civic participation and individuality, though libertarian strands accept withdrawal; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Mill warns of conformity pressure from mass opinion, but individualists do not generally hold that culture reproduces a social order; inferred as split.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim outside the individualist tradition; no documented position, so inferred as neutral.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Classical liberalism holds that trade and investment benefit poor countries, rejecting dependency-style explanations; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Equal rights and careers open to talent run against reserving offices by birth origin; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Concerns relations between communist parties, which individualism does not address; neutral inference.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Classical liberals favour open trade and foreign investment as tools of development; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Individual rights rather than collective territorial claims are the liberal individualist focus; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Equal individual rights regardless of descent contradict group-based political leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Individualists oppose fascism as the subordination of the individual to the state, but a constitutional founding value is not a documented demand; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Hayek argued that collectivist planning in fascism and socialism share a common root, and individualists generally condemn both as subordinating the individual.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Slavery negates individual self-ownership, so individualists tend to accept it as the central cause; a historical question outside the doctrine, inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Adherents split between free-speech and anti-state-symbol positions; inferred as neutral.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Equal treatment of individuals regardless of sex implies equal public attention; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Equal protection of individuals regardless of sex implies symmetry; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Liberal individualism claims universal individual rights, so rejects civilizational relativism about institutions; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Liberal individualism demands civilian, constitutional control of force and distrusts military political roles.

paid-care-work.rationale: Individualists favour contract and market pricing over state-mandated payment for household work; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the view that obligations arise from consent rather than birth, though Mill-style individualists value family affection.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; Mill favoured competitive examination for the civil service in other writings, but the classical strand is not unified on it.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from classical liberal support for free contract and free movement of capital.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Free ending of a voluntary association follows from the harm principle and individual autonomy over one's life.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from Hayek's and Mill's preference for representatives using independent judgment rather than binding mandates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from classical liberal preference for private voluntary provision, though some individualists accept state schemes.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Self-ownership and private property rights, central to the libertarian strand, conflict with communal or use-only land tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Limited government under constitutional constraints is a core classical liberal position, including legislative control of taxation.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from distrust of enforced conformity and restriction of individual choice, though a common language is not opposed in itself.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from property rights and free contract that do not depend on nationality.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from the focus on equal rules and individual treatment rather than group outcomes, as in Hayek's equal rules.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the view that individuals judge their own good and the state or critics should not impose tastes, though Mill criticised conformity in taste.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from classical liberal scepticism of state coercion and war, which would extend to covert foreign interventions.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from rejection of coercion against self-governing peoples and states beyond preventing harm.

corporate-influence.rationale: Liberal individualists dislike both concentrated power and state meddling, and are split on how to tackle lobbying; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: freedom of association and expression favours open funding of civil society, though some liberals accept limits on foreign state money.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: family choices are private and the state steering them with incentives conflicts with limited government.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from strong property rights and freedom of movement, which locals' veto over purchases would violate.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: a state job guarantee is state direction of labour and conflicts with limited government and voluntary exchange.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred from the Kantian and classical-liberal tradition, which links free institutions to peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: in the Lockean and libertarian traditions authority rests on consent, so there is no automatic duty to obey.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed directly; liberals are divided between non-intervention and rights-based intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Voluntary association is endorsed but the form of union is not addressed.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Individualism judges people as individuals with equal rights, not as members of ethnic or religious groups, so group conspiracy claims conflict with it.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: libertarian and some liberal strands would privatise marriage as a contract rather than a state-conferred status.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: accountable, limited government is served by citizens being able to see what the state does.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed; individualists leave where goods are made to voluntary exchange.

informal-organisation.rationale: Mill and Hayek defend voluntary association of any kind and do not prescribe a form of organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed; liberals are split between national constitutional supremacy and international human-rights courts.

religious-nation.rationale: Mill and the liberal tradition defend freedom of conscience and separate belief from state membership, so a religion-defined nation conflicts with it.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: individualists favour equal rules over hierarchy and ritual submission, though the topic is outside the sources.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Individualism is indifferent to regional units; low taxation favours keeping revenue, but the focus is the individual, so it is split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Hayek and the libertarian tradition defend private property and reject collective ownership of the means of production as planning.

defeat-communism.rationale: Hayek treats central planning as a threat to liberty, so adherents lean against communism, though many oppose crusades; inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: classical liberals prefer competition and choice among providers over state monopoly, even where funding is public.

religion-illusion.rationale: Mill defends freedom of belief and unbelief; the claim that religion is mere illusion is not an individualist tenet, so the answer is inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Hayek credits competition and the market order with creating wealth and widening opportunity.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Individualists seek equal rights under law, not transformation of the economy; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: domestic arrangements are for individuals and families to choose, not for public provision.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Mill opposes enforced custom and conformity; official purging of words is coercion over private speech.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from rule of law and respect for agreements, which classical liberals extend to government commitments.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Voluntary communes are allowed, but reorganising society into compulsory common property conflicts with self-ownership; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: State steering of population movements is central planning and coercion, which Hayek and the harm principle reject.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: individualists side with market-based liberalism rather than a third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Individual rights, not collective historical claims, are the unit of moral concern; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; this is a factual claim about history that individualists reject, though they would defend the freedom to say it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Mill's harm principle limits coercion to preventing harm to others, so private consensual conduct should not be criminal.

suppress-opposition.rationale: On Liberty defends freedom of association and of opinion, and says the state may not suppress dissent to preserve order.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: On Liberty argues against punishing opinions, including religious ones, so adherents reject punishment of blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not addressed; liberal individualism opposes colonial rule over others without consent, inferred from consent theory.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; religious duties imposed on every person conflict with individual autonomy, inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; individualists distrust force but accept resistance to tyranny on Lockean grounds; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Individuals deciding for themselves fits, but individualists distrust collective decision-making; adherents split.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Individualism analyses people as individuals, not through overlapping group categories; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Autonomy over one's own identity fits, though legal recognition is a state matter; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Autonomy over one's own life is a core individualist and libertarian claim.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not addressed; individualists could say either.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation theory is Marxist; individualists defend market work as voluntary; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the view that people should be judged as individuals, not as members of religions.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Liberal theory grounds authority in individual consent, not divine right, though Locke used religious language.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Free expression and dress favour individual choice, though some limits on officials are accepted; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Freedom of contract and protection from harm pull in opposite directions; adherents split.

social-market-economy.rationale: The scope covers classical-liberal views; it favours laissez-faire and limited government over social protection; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Libertarian strands distrust standing armies, but mainstream liberalism accepts defence; inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal acceptance of unequal outcomes from free exchange.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal distrust of entangling alliances.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Liberal individualism rejects hereditary privilege in favour of individual merit and rights; succession by birth conflicts with that.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Voluntary mutual banks suit individualists but cost-price rules are contested; adherents split.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred; classical liberals disfavour state borrowing but also lender-imposed conditions, so adherents split.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred from Mill and Locke: property was often tied to voting historically, but individual rights imply equal votes.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not addressed; individualists focus on individual rights rather than collective structures of domination.

reification.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal view that markets coordinate free individuals without distorting social relations.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from classical liberalism's defence of property rights and of formal freedoms as real.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Hayek's liberal individualism rests on rule of law: government by general, known rules rather than discretion.

racial-franchise.rationale: Individualism grounds rights in the individual, not group membership, so a racial franchise contradicts it.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed; individualists may favour online participation but not as a defining position.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the liberal demand that government be accountable to individuals and limited.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Individualism holds that coercion is justified only to prevent harm, so restricting adults' marriages is rejected.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Individuals may choose where to shop, yet it opposes prejudice by creed; adherents split.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Individualists split between distrust of collective decisions and openness to participatory institutions; the sources do not address it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from the stress on individual conscience and freedom of thought, which favours believers rethinking doctrine for themselves.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Classical strands see wealth as the result of voluntary exchange and the main threat to liberty as the state; adherents differ, so this is inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Mill's On Liberty defends unconventional ways of life and bars coercion not aimed at preventing harm to others.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Individualism rejects state imposition of belief and the state-enforced conformity that promoting atheism would require.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Mainstream classical liberal individualism keeps a state to protect rights; only individualist anarchist strands would abolish police and prisons.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; individualism's distrust of coercion cuts both ways on enforced power sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the libertarian preference for voluntary provision over compulsory state programs.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from distrust of concentrated political power; not a defining issue.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; delegation expands individual choice but departs from the standard representative model.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; no principle to infer from.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Individual rights favour equal eligibility, but freedom of association lets religious bodies set their own rules.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on individual autonomy of each spouse, as in Mill's liberal tradition.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; individualists are split between rights of residents and local-property-based franchise.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: price caps override free contract between landlord and tenant, which classical liberal individualism resists.

abolish-ip.rationale: Contested within the tradition: Lockean property thinkers defend patents and copyright, while Tucker-style and left-libertarian strands reject them.

uniformed-youth.rationale: State-organised drilled youth movements are enforced conformity, which individualism opposes.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Defence posture is not addressed by individualism.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from distrust of large state power and standing military establishments in classical liberalism; adherents differ.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed; recognition acts are state commemoration, on which individualists are split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred: in the Lockean tradition income from property is as legitimate as wages, so ownership need not be penalised.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from Locke's natural right to defend oneself and others, central to individual rights.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred: individualism treats the person, not the nation, as the basic unit and is wary of collective identity myths.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; individualists hold varied views on gender theory.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from its treatment of persons as individuals rather than members of fixed group categories.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: sacrificing the individual to the nation runs against individualist priorities.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: individualism limits politics to protecting rights, not to cosmic struggle between good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; diaspora policy is not part of the doctrine.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not addressed; cultural renewal as a national project is neither required nor forbidden.

god-not-male.rationale: Religious language is a matter of individual conscience for individualists.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Individualists defend freedom of conscience and take no common stance on religious texts.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Reserving economic life by group membership violates equal individual rights and free exchange, central to the liberal individualist tradition.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: drawing territory around a people is collective-group politics, which individualism does not endorse.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the freedom-of-association strand of liberal individualism: voluntary bodies should stand apart from the state.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: individualists generally do not treat class power as the test of a just society and focus on individual rights instead.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal preference for voluntary or private provision over state ownership; new-liberal strands differ.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the liberal concern to check concentrated power, which bicameral and divided institutions serve.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: individualism favours individual private property over collective or communal ownership of the means of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Individualism has no stated view on municipal confederation; the structure of government is secondary to individual rights.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred: wages set by individual contract rather than by a family-needs standard fits the classical individualist view.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred from the individualist and libertarian view that competent adults should decide on their own risks and treatment.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Individualists would welcome the research but split on government funding versus private effort, so the sources settle nothing.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the individualist defence of private conduct and distrust of state surveillance of individuals.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from Mill's defence of freedom of thought and expression and of a private sphere beyond social or state coercion.

person-over-state.rationale: Individualism puts the individual's autonomy and rights ahead of the state's demands, and Mill's harm principle bars using a person merely for the community's ends.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Individualism leaves the nature of the person to each individual; adherents range from religious to secular.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Individualism has no stated view on regional autonomy; it cares about limits on power at every level, not who holds it.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from the liberal and libertarian preference for permitting technology unless harm to others is shown.

dense-cities.rationale: Not a topic individualist sources address; adherents prize individual choice of where to live, so it is genuinely split.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Individualism treats the person, not the group, as the unit of political concern and Hayek opposes collectivist thinking, so organising by racial group is resisted.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred: individualists value what a person chooses and achieves over inherited group membership, so pride in ancestry is not their ground.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from the liberal tradition's limits on state power and concern for individual rights, which weigh against wars of choice.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred from the individualist rejection of collective identities: people are individuals first, so a shared language does not bind them into one nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Individualism treats citizens as equal individuals, not members of religious blocs, and Mill and the liberal tradition oppose group-defined political rights.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: the tradition distrusts nationalist conspiracy narratives that subordinate the individual to a collective cause.

free-public-college.rationale: Mainstream classical individualists oppose subsidising others' education through taxation, though new liberals disagree.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Libertarian-leaning strands favour property rights and market pricing of harm, while others reject new taxes; adherents are split.

future-generations.rationale: Individualists dispute duties to people who do not yet exist, and the sources do not settle it.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the individualist rejection of group-based generalisations about character, which treats people as individuals, not as a gender.

arms-reduction.rationale: Classical liberalism distrusts standing armies and state power, and Hayek and Mill favour limiting state force, though a minimal state keeps defence.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from liberal distrust of secret state action, an argument the SEP entry on liberalism ties to limits on power.

capital-controls.rationale: Individualist liberalism holds that people may use their property freely, and Hayek and the libertarian tradition oppose state controls on capital movement.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Locke grounds a state monopoly of force, but gun-rights libertarians dissent; adherents are split.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Individual conscience over state demands fits Mill's harm principle and libertarian anti-war strands; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Freedom of contract favours individual agreements, and Hayek criticised union privileges; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Classical individualists resist state income top-ups, though some new liberals accept them; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The classical tradition distrusts state discretion and favours rules limiting government; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from classical liberal confidence in free trade and existing market rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Classical liberals favour constitutional reform over destroying the state; individualist anarchists dissent.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Hayek's true individualism rejects central design and favours spontaneous order and experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Property-rights strands would price nature while others reject it; adherents are split.

sacred-nation.rationale: Individualism ranks the individual above collective entities such as the nation; the sacred framing is rejected by inference.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Borrowers are held to their contracts and costs fall on taxpayers; inferred from classical liberalism.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Individualists see exchange as voluntary and not exploitative by region; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Natural rights traditions ground individual rights in a common human nature, though transhumanist libertarians dissent; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: State-funded media conflicts with limited government and voluntary provision; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Individualism defends freedom of belief but takes no view on whether religions share one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred: the classical strand opposes state price-setting and favours voluntary exchange.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Individualists are split between limited-state deterrence and anti-war or anti-state views.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: individualism favours individual political choice over class-based group identity, though it permits free association.

ban-fgm.rationale: Mill's harm principle justifies prohibiting non-consensual bodily harm to others, including children.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Liberal individualism holds that individuals have equal rights regardless of sex, including property.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Individualism has no view on language classification.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Libertarian individualism holds that physical harm to another's property is a rights violation to be redressed through liability.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: individualism rejects inherited or group authority over individuals in lawmaking.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Placing another value above individual liberty contradicts individualism's priority on liberty, which Mill limits only by harm to others.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred: individualism distrusts rigid state rules over individual circumstances.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred: individualism opposes state-imposed requirements on how people live, though it permits private expectations.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Individualists hold that freedom of association includes the freedom not to join, so compulsory membership as a condition of work violates individual choice.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: individualists are split between protecting the integrity of a limited state's mandate and wariness of state-imposed barriers; not addressed.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Classical liberal individualism, from Locke on, holds that the state should not privilege one religious view over another.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred: individualists value elections but stress limits on majorities, as Mill and Tocqueville did, so they are split on a purely procedural test.

premarital-sex.rationale: Mill's On Liberty defends unconventional ways of life where no harm to others results, which covers private sexual choices.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Individualism holds that coercion is justified only to prevent harm to others and defends freedom of expression, which shutdowns violate.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: Hayek and Friedman-style classical liberals favoured a minimum-income or negative-income-tax scheme, though other individualists reject any welfare state.

women-suffrage.rationale: Individualism grounds rights in the individual, and Mill argued for women's suffrage and equality in The Subjection of Women.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: individualists defend freedom of belief and are split on whether religion as such is a major cause of oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from its treatment of persons as individuals rather than as members of racial groups; not addressed directly.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: individualists favour equal rights under law but distrust new state bureaucracies, so are wary of dedicated agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Locke's labour-based account of property that classical individualists inherit; the sources opened do not state it for the strand as a whole.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred: individualists split between protecting individual rights through international law and distrusting supranational authority.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from Mill's defence of individual judgment against custom and authority; he takes no formal stand on scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from its universal individual rights, which would not allow group customs to override a woman's equal rights.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Hayek argues against central planning, and individualists distrust a state-run economy; defending one runs against the strand.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from its liberal preference for individuals choosing their rulers directly; the sources do not discuss indirect election.

national-church-status.rationale: Liberal tradition from Locke on holds that the state should not privilege a church, treating belief as a matter for the individual.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from its priority of individual over group rights; it would not give a territory autonomy by ethnicity.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from its consent-based view of political authority; the sources do not discuss plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address colonial borders and the strand gives no common view.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from Mill's 'experiments of living': individuals choose their own lifestyles, so no ideal is imposed.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its preference for freedom of movement and settlement and its suspicion of group-based restrictions.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: individualists reject conscription as coercion of the person; the statement allows 'neither', which fits.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from its priority of the individual over collective, ancestral claims.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Due process and protection of individual rights against the state are central to the liberal individualist tradition.

close-ties-china.rationale: Foreign alignment is not addressed by the doctrine, inferred as neutral.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of collective ethnic claims; state action on behalf of a nation is not an individual-rights aim.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Mainstream classical-liberal strands favour private appropriation, though left-libertarians dissent; inferred.

self-ownership.rationale: Libertarian and liberal individualism treat each person's rights over their own body and labour as foundational.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from its general support for low taxes and limited government; consumption taxes are not specifically discussed.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Adherents are split between minimal safety nets, targeted aid and no welfare state.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from its distrust of concentrated personal power and its defence of pluralism and associations.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Classical liberal individualists oppose state-granted privileges as coercive and distorting; Hayek's essay criticises such favours.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from its stress on freedom of conscience and individual choice over group identity.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from its stress on individual choice over inherited norms and enforced conformity.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Individual autonomy and equal liberty, including leaving marriage, are defended in Mill's On Liberty.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from its preference for private over state ownership and from free trade in resources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Mainstream classical-liberal individualism judges fairness by voluntary, rights-respecting process rather than outcome patterns; inferred from the entitlement view in the libertarian tradition.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from classical liberal scepticism of taxes beyond protective purposes and of state steering of markets.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Individualism as such does not address racism; adherents split on whether structural effects remain, so no side is implied.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Locke's natural-rights strand supports resisting unjust law while Mill's harm-principle strand stresses proper procedure and reform, so adherents are split.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Individualists welcome technology but dislike planned social engineering of work; neither side is implied.

multipolar-world.rationale: The tradition is about individuals, not the balance of world powers; no position is implied.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal and Hayekian emphasis on subjective, dispersed individual valuation over any single objective source of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Individualism neither favours nor opposes patriotism; Hayek-style individualists are wary of collective loyalties, but adherents are split.

material-over-identity.rationale: Individualism is indifferent to left priorities; it defends individual rights of both economic and cultural kinds.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from individualist opposition to central direction of the economy and concentrated one-party power over individuals.

missingStatements.text: Social pressure to conform to custom does as much harm to human development as the law does, and eccentric ways of living should be encouraged.
missingStatements.rationale: Mill argues in On Liberty ch. III that custom stifles individuality and that eccentricity is valuable, a defining claim not captured by the legal-limit statements.

notes: Individualist anarchists and left-libertarians would answer economic items differently; the profile follows the mainstream liberal strand.
